transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I barely sleep anymore. I lie there hearing rain or thinking about the bluff giving way, and when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up sweaty from dreams. Then I go to the call center feeling like I never slept at all.
Did something frightening or dangerous happen to you before these sleep problems started?
Yeah. Things from that trail keep coming back out of nowhere—the sound of rocks sliding, my leg pinned under me. For a minute I’m not even at my desk anymore; it feels like I’m back there.
Have you been avoiding reminders of the trail or what happened there?
Yeah. I won’t go anywhere near the coast trails now. And I’ve been dodging texts from my hiking buddies—just talking about going out there makes my chest tighten.
How long have these problems been going on since the accident?
About four months now—since I got trapped when the bluff trail collapsed.
Have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled since the accident?
I’m not really sure what you mean by constantly on guard. I haven’t really noticed anything specific like that.
Since the accident, have you been jumpier than usual—for example, getting startled easily by sudden sounds or movements?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself getting startled more than usual.
Since the accident, have you felt unusually watchful or on guard?
No, I wouldn’t say I’ve felt especially watchful or on guard.
Since the accident, have you been blaming yourself or feeling guilty about what happened?
Yeah. I keep thinking I was stupid and careless for being out there alone. And now I feel like if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad is going to happen.
Since the accident, have you been feeling a lot of fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame?
Yeah. Most days I feel scared, and honestly embarrassed too—like people can tell I messed up, like I’m not as tough as I used to act.
Since the accident, have you found yourself believing that the world is unsafe or that you can’t really trust yourself anymore?
Yeah. I keep thinking I was stupid for being out there alone, and it feels like if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad is going to happen.
Have these problems made it harder for you to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah. My work’s slipped—I missed important CRM notes and got written up after a call escalation. I’m worried I messed up my chance to move toward team lead. And I’ve fallen behind on studying for my GED because I’m exhausted and I’ve been avoiding the people I used to hike with.
